parts:
Hi All,

I need to use the R function digamma(), but it's not supported by Nimble. So, before I go about trying to write a new nimbleFunction myself, I was wondering if anyone had a Nimble digamma function already that I could use. If not, I'd also appreciate any ideas about the best way to approximate it in nimble.

Any ideas would be greatly appreciated, of course!

Sincerely,

Chris

messages.author: 0c7ffcac30445989
messages.subject: Re: digamma
parts:
Apologies for the rapid double post, but I wanted to post my working solution here. The following is a cheap approximation to the digamma function good to 2 or 3 decimal places based on what I've tried so far. Any improvements on accuracy would be very welcome as would any other comments/criticisms that might improve the function.

Thanks,

C

nimbleDigamma <- nimbleFunction(
   run = function(X = double(1)){
      t_ <- seq(1e-7,max(X)+10,0.0001)
      output <- c()
      for(x in X){
         di_y <- sum( ( (exp(-t_)/t_) - (exp(-x * t_) / (1 - exp(-t_))) ) * 0.0001 )
         output <- c(output, di_y)
      }
      returnType(double(1))
      return(output)
   }
)

Perry
-------

library(nimble)

                        returnType = double())

code <- nimbleCode({
    b ~ dexp(1)
    a <- Rdigamma(b)
})

model <- nimbleModel(code, calculate = FALSE)
    
cmodel <- compileNimble(model)

cmodel$simulate()
cmodel$b
cmodel$a
digamma(cmodel$b)

I think you want:

nimDigamma <- nimbleFunction(
   run = function(X = double(0)){
...
 
since you are passing scalars to nimDigamma, and

returnType(double(0))

since you are returning to a scalar (e.g. rho[j]).  On the other hand you are constructing a vector (output), but assigning it to scalars (rho[j]).

I don't totally follow what you want, but double(1) means vector and double(0) means scalar, and in model code the type on the left-hand side must match the return type of the function on the right-hand side.

Also the

for(x in X){
...

will not work in compilation.  For loops only take sequential integer ranges at this point in development.

Let me know if that helps you iron it out or if something is still not right.
